summary.name: Claude Code Hooks Complete Guide
summary.one_liner: A detailed reference guide to Claude Code hooks, covering the full event lifecycle, exit-code and JSON decision protocol, tool matchers, settings.json layering, worked examples, and security considerations.
use_cases: Blocking dangerous shell commands in Claude Code
Auto-formatting files after Claude edits them
Protecting secret or credential files from edits
Logging every tool call for audit
Preventing Claude from stopping until tests pass
Injecting git state or policy context at session start
summary.what_it_does: The guide walks through the Claude Code hook lifecycle, listing events such as PreToolUse, PostToolUse, UserPromptSubmit, Stop, SubagentStop, SessionStart and PreCompact, and when each fires. It explains the two return channels: exit codes (for example, exit 2 to block) and JSON output with allow, deny, ask and defer decisions. It covers tool matchers, including the regex rules and MCP tool name pitfalls, and where hook definitions live in the settings.json hierarchy. It also includes copy-ready examples for formatting, blocking, audit logging, turn guards and context injection, along with a discussion of the security model.
notable: Full table of roughly thirty hook events grouped by lifecycle phase, with matcher fields
Explains exit code 2 versus JSON decision shapes, including PreToolUse permissionDecision values
Notes that a PreToolUse deny is evaluated before permission-mode checks and hooks can only tighten access
Documents the regex trap when matching MCP tool names
caveats: The set of hook events changes over time; the official Claude Code hooks reference is stated to be authoritative
Hooks run as arbitrary commands with the user's shell privileges, so security review is needed
A Stop hook that always blocks can loop forever, according to the page
